## 👋 Hello, this is Dingjin.

*Explore important [research](projects_intro.qmd) questions using robust [datasets](datasets_intro.qmd) and rigorous [methods](methods_intro.qmd) under well-defined [assumptions](methods_assumptions.qmd).*

---

I study how forests store carbon, how they respond to climate extremes, and how much they cool our cities. My work asks questions such as: *Can a global biomass map be trusted to report the carbon in a local forest? Which forests hold their biomass through drought? Why do some urban forests cool their surroundings far more than others?* Read more in the [Research](projects_intro.qmd) section.

To answer them, I combine field inventories (FIA, NEON) with airborne, spaceborne and terrestrial LiDAR and multi-decadal satellite records — see [Datasets](datasets_intro.qmd) — and analyze them with statistical models, interpretable machine learning and process-based models — see [Methods](methods_intro.qmd).

**Latest:** I presented a talk on urban forest cooling and a poster on biomass-map bias at the [SAF National Convention](news.qmd) (Oct 2026), and my paper on climate extremes and productivity variability in Central Asia is out in [*Environmental Research Letters*](https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/ae6dd4).
